extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, counsel and parties prosecuting or defending Section 337 investigations before the ITC and on appeal to the Federal Circuit
extracted.subtask_description: Legal standards and evidentiary rules for proving the Section 337 'domestic industry' requirement (technical and economic prongs) in ITC investigations and appeals, including when and how investments may be aggregated or must be allocated patent-by-patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 337 prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 337 prohibits '[t]he importation into the United States, the sale for importation, or the sale within the United States after importation' of articles that infringe a U.S. patent. (19 U.S.C. § 1337(a)(1)(B)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the substantive acts that can form the basis of a Section 337 investigation. It is background to the domestic industry inquiry but defines the actionable conduct the Commission may enjoin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic industry requirement (19 U.S.C. § 1337(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain relief under section 337 a complainant must show that 'an industry in the United States, relating to the articles protected by the patent . . . exists or is in the process of being established.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The domestic industry requirement has two prongs: a technical prong (products are protected by the asserted patent) and an economic prong (significant/substantial investments). The complainant bears the burden of proving the existence of such a domestic industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical prong (relating to articles protected by the patent)
rubrics_metrics.description: The technical prong requires the complainant to show that its domestic industry products are 'protected by the patent' at issue (i.e., the products practice the asserted patent claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is no dispute about the technical prong, the inquiry focuses on the economic prong. The technical prong ties the claimed patent to the complainant’s domestic products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic prong statutory categories (§ 1337(a)(3)(A)–(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: The economic prong can be satisfied by showing, 'with respect to the articles protected by the patent,' (A) 'significant investment in plant and equipment,' (B) 'significant employment of labor or capital,' or (C) 'substantial investment in its exploitation, including engineering, research and development, or licensing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are alternative ways to establish the economic prong. A complainant may rely on one or more of these categories to demonstrate a domestic industry relating to the asserted patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investments must be with respect to articles protected by each asserted patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 337(a)(2) and (a)(3) tie the domestic industry to products 'protected by the patent' and require the complainant to show significant or substantial expenditures 'with respect to the articles protected by the patent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where multiple patents and multiple products are at issue, the complainant must provide sufficient evidence to evaluate the significance of investments with respect to each asserted patent; failing to do so precludes the Commission from determining whether the statutory categories are met for each patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation requirement / limits on aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: A complainant who aggregates investments across domestic products that practice different patents 'failed to provide the Commission with an adequate basis to evaluate the investments and the significance of those investments with respect to each asserted patent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregating investments across products that practice different patents is problematic; complainants must provide a reasonable allocation method to estimate how much of their investments are attributable to each asserted patent or product group, or otherwise present evidence sufficient to show the requirement is met for each patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grouping when products all practice same patent
rubrics_metrics.description: When all the domestic industry products practice the same patent, it is permissible to group different products together and use the entire product group to assess expenditures—for example, 'expenses on research and development of a specific article need not be broken down into the amount related to any specific patents' if the activities are directed towards articles that incorporate the patented technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No patent-by-patent allocation is required in that scenario because the group as a whole relates to the asserted patent; grouping is appropriate only where the grouped products actually practice the same patent(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for substantial overlap (single-industry showing)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is 'substantial overlap' among products practicing multiple asserted patents such that exploitation of the patents results in production of a single commercial product, a complainant may establish a single domestic industry rather than separate industries for each patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exception (e.g., Certain DRAMs) depends on record evidence showing substantial overlap (e.g., same processes/equipment, products effectively a single commercial product). Post‑1988 statutory amendments limit DRAMs' applicability; the exception is fact-specific and not a free pass for aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: R&D investments under (a)(3)(C) must pertain to products covered by the asserted patent
rubrics_metrics.description: To satisfy section 337(a)(3)(C), a complainant's research and development activities must 'pertain to products that are covered by the patent that is being asserted.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precedent (e.g., Interdigital) requires that R&D expenditures be tied to products covered by the asserted patent(s); generalized R&D not shown to relate to patented products will not carry the economic prong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary sufficiency and form of allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The complainant is required to identify, in some manner, how much of its investment in each statutory category was attributable to each group of products or patents; presenting only aggregate numbers for many products practicing different patents 'effectively precludes the Commission from quantifying the amounts of the investments in each statutory category.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential allocation methods (e.g., revenue-based breakdowns) may be acceptable if properly in the evidentiary record and tied to the products/patents; summary or demonstrative materials excluded as substantive evidence cannot be relied on. The Commission lacks license to perform the allocation sua sponte without sufficient record evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility, corroboration, and weight of testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Sworn witness testimony directed to the domestic industry requirement may be credited without documentary corroboration, but the testimony must be explained or corroborated sufficiently; unsupported or unexplained estimates are not enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ALJ’s credibility determinations and weighing of evidence are entitled to great weight. Testimony that merely 'estimated' figures without documentary support or an explanation may be found unreliable. Prior Commission decisions note testimony can be credited absent written records, but those cases involved corroboration or an explanation of method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof on complainant
rubrics_metrics.description: It was 'Zircon’s burden to prove the existence of a domestic industry relating to articles protected by each of its patents' and to show that its investments in plant and equipment, labor or capital, and/or research and development were significant or substantial under 19 U.S.C. § 1337(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainants must present sufficient, allocable evidence for each asserted patent. Failure to make the required showing results in denial of relief without reaching infringement/invalidity issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural preservation and admissibility of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence excluded by an ALJ (e.g., by motion in limine) is not necessarily part of the evidentiary record for proving domestic industry; administrative-record pleadings differ from evidence admissible at hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties cannot rely on excluded declarations or exhibits on appeal if they did not preserve or appeal the ALJ’s exclusion; citing an exhibit in a witness statement as a demonstrative does not admit it as substantive evidence. Parties should ensure allocative evidence is offered and admitted at the hearing stage.
